interpretation_rules.recommended_language: The thermogram is consistent with a sequence of membrane transitions; separate process models and orthogonal morphology measurements are needed before reporting one affinity or stoichiometry.

interpretation_rules.trigger: apparent membrane partition coefficient changes with ligand concentration or vesicle size
interpretation_rules.conclusion: The membrane may be perturbed or the partition process may depend on curvature, packing, charge, or transbilayer equilibration; the apparent parameter is not automatically intrinsic.
interpretation_rules.recommended_language: The reported partition parameter is conditional on membrane composition, curvature, coverage, and equilibration timescale; intrinsic values require an explicit model and concentration-series validation.

interpretation_rules.trigger: fitted enthalpy or curve shape changes with stirring rate, paddle geometry, or mixing intensity
interpretation_rules.conclusion: Mixing-dependent aggregation, unfolding, incompetent fractions, or incomplete reaction may be contaminating the apparent binding heat.
interpretation_rules.recommended_language: The thermodynamic parameters are mixing-condition dependent until paddle geometry, stirring rate, sample integrity, and equilibration are controlled.

interpretation_rules.trigger: heat is generated by dilution of an oligomer into lower concentration
interpretation_rules.conclusion: The experiment can report self-association/dissociation thermodynamics, but only with an oligomerization model and an independently justified dilution baseline.
interpretation_rules.recommended_language: The dilution heats are consistent with an oligomer–monomer equilibrium under the stated self-association model; a conventional heterobinding fit is not appropriate.

interpretation_rules.trigger: ligand length, linkage, or subsite occupancy changes carbohydrate-binding enthalpy
interpretation_rules.conclusion: The ligand may change contact architecture or engage multiple subsites; affinity and enthalpy differences should not be interpreted as independent additive contacts without structural support.
interpretation_rules.recommended_language: The saccharide series indicates ligand-dependent contact architecture; subsite assignments require structural, mutational, or orthogonal validation.

interpretation_rules.trigger: a labeled ligand gives a different enthalpy or curve from the native ligand
interpretation_rules.conclusion: The label may alter complex geometry, binding mode, local solvation, or effective species concentration; the discrepancy is not necessarily instrument noise.
interpretation_rules.recommended_language: Label-dependent thermodynamics indicate that the modified ligand may form a different ensemble or complex; native and labeled parameters should be compared as distinct experiments.

interpretation_rules.trigger: metal-ion ITC involves buffers, chelators, redox-active ions, hydrolysis, or precipitation
interpretation_rules.conclusion: The measured K_ITC and ΔH_ITC may include metal-buffer/chelator equilibria and proton competition; condition-independent parameters require explicit speciation analysis.
interpretation_rules.recommended_language: The apparent metal-binding thermodynamics are conditional on metal speciation and buffer competition; post hoc correction or a validated metal-delivery complex is required for intrinsic parameters.

interpretation_rules.trigger: a classical binding equation fits ITC data well but the system has large solvation, stacking, folding, or concentration-dependent pre-equilibria
interpretation_rules.conclusion: Good residuals do not establish that the classical model captures all thermodynamic state variables or that the fitted parameters have a unique mechanistic meaning.
interpretation_rules.recommended_language: The classical model describes the measured curve under the chosen conditions, but additional solvation or conformational equilibria may be folded into the apparent parameters.

interpretation_rules.trigger: fitted stoichiometry is implausible and ligand purity is uncertain
interpretation_rules.conclusion: Impurities can distort apparent enthalpy and stoichiometry; forcing n to an expected value can produce inaccurate thermodynamic parameters.
interpretation_rules.recommended_language: Verify ligand identity and purity and test the concentration model before constraining or manually changing stoichiometry.

interpretation_rules.trigger: ΔCp from nucleic-acid duplex formation varies with sequence, salt, or temperature
interpretation_rules.conclusion: Residual single-strand stacking and other coupled pre-equilibria may dominate the observed ΔCp; it should not automatically be assigned to duplex interface hydration.
interpretation_rules.recommended_language: The observed ΔCp includes coupled strand-structure contributions under these conditions; single-strand melting or folding controls are needed for an intrinsic duplex interpretation.

interpretation_rules.trigger: direct ITC isotherm is nearly vertical because Kd is in the single-digit nanomolar range
interpretation_rules.conclusion: The direct titration may constrain ΔH but not Kd accurately; displacement ITC, concentration reduction, or an orthogonal equilibrium method is preferable.
interpretation_rules.recommended_language: The interaction is tighter than the direct ITC design can resolve reliably; the affinity estimate should come from an alternative or displacement design.

language_patterns.text: The isotherm is consistent with a single dominant binding transition under these conditions. The fitted affinity and enthalpy are well supported by the curve shape, while the stoichiometry is consistent with the assumed model.

The experiment clearly supports high-affinity binding, but the transition is too steep to localize Kd precisely. The fitted Kd should therefore be treated as an approximate value or bound rather than a precise measurement.

The low-c design provides limited information on stoichiometry. Affinity may still be constrained by the titration range, but n and ΔH should not be interpreted independently without additional information.
The weak calorimetric signal limits what can be concluded from ITC at this temperature. This does not by itself indicate absence of binding.
Binding is endothermic but thermodynamically favorable because the favorable entropy term outweighs the enthalpic penalty.
Binding is enthalpically favorable. The calorimetry alone does not uniquely identify the molecular origin of this enthalpy.
The data are consistent with heterogeneous or multisite binding, but the individual microscopic affinities are not well resolved by this experiment.
The residuals contain systematic structure, indicating that the fitted model or data treatment does not fully describe the experiment.

The fitted stoichiometry differs from the nominal expectation. Possible explanations include concentration error, inactive material, genuine functional valence, heterogeneous accessibility, or model mismatch.
No heat-associated binding was detected under the tested conditions. This is not equivalent to proving that the molecules do not interact.
The experiment contains features that are atypical for the fitted binding model, so the quantitative parameters should be treated cautiously even if the data qualitatively support an interaction.

The mutation changes the measured affinity relative to wild type. Mechanistic interpretation is strongest if the samples are comparably folded and the affinity change agrees with independent structural, kinetic, or functional evidence.
The similar affinities mask different thermodynamic partitions, with enthalpy and entropy compensating to produce comparable binding free energies.
The temperature dependence of the binding enthalpy can provide a heat-capacity change if the same equilibrium model remains valid across the temperature series.
The reported affinity is obtained from a coupled competition experiment and therefore depends on the independently known thermodynamics of the competing ligand.
